recipe: To replace every property value of an object type with one type, use a generic mapped type: `type Remap<T, X> = { [K in keyof T]: X }`. Keys and their modifiers are preserved.
trigger_condition: You need to transform an object type by replacing all its property values with a single type.
evidence: craft a type (`PresentDeliveryList`) that takes an object type as an input and then replaces the values at each property with an `Address`
source_name: TypeHero: Advent of TypeScript 2023, Day Four
_original_recipe: When you need to replace all property values in an object type with a specific type, create a generic type that takes the object type as input and maps each property to the target type.
_review_reason: recipe did not name the mechanism; state the general mapped-type technique without the challenge's Address type

recipe: Use a generic type when the set of properties is unknown at compile time, so the type adapts to whatever object is passed in.
trigger_condition: The properties of the input object are not known in advance and vary between usage sites.
evidence: We don't know in advance what properties will be provided, which is why it needs to be a generic type.
